===Pronunciation===

===Noun===
{{en-noun|-|+}}

# {{lb|en|mathematics}} The mathematical theory of [[set]]s.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1972|author=Peter W. Zehna; Robert Leo Johnson|title=Elements of '''Set Theory'''|publisher=w:Allyn & Bacon|pageurl=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=FfruAAAAMAAJ&q=%22set+theory%22%7C%22set+theories%22&dq=%22set+theory%22%7C%22set+theories%22&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwjW4omGjI_cAhUBS7wKHRYYAbkQ6AEIzAEwGw|page=4
|passage=We mentioned previously that certain paradoxes in '''set theory''' arose shortly after Cantor's works were published.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1984|author=Robert Goldblatt|title=Topoi, the categorial analysis of logic|url=http://ebooks.library.cornell.edu/cgi/t/text/pageviewer-idx?c=math;cc=math;idno=gold010;q1=Heyting%20algebra;view=image;seq=26;size=100;page=root|page=9
|passage=The above argument, known as Russell's Paradox, was discovered by Bertrand Russell in 1901. '''Set theory''' itself began a few decades earlier with the work of George Cantor.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1994|author=Yiannis N. Moschovakis|title=Notes on '''Set Theory'''|pageurl=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=ndx0_6VCypcC&pg=PA239&dq=%22set+theories%22&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwjxnra5jY_cAhWIT7wKHV5QA_wQ6AEIfjAQ#v=onepage&q=%22set%20theories%22&f=false|page=239|publisher=Springer
|passage=The serious study of ''models'' of axiomatic '''set theories''' depends heavily on methods from ''mathematical logic'' which are outside the scope of these Notes.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=M. Randall Holmes; Thomas Forster; Thierry Libert|chapter=Alternative '''Set Theories'''|editors=w:Dov M. Gabbay; Akihiro Kanimori; John Woods|title=Sets and Extensions in the Twentieth Century|publisher=Elsevier|location=North-Holland|pageurl=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=RBrWwKVbmMUC&pg=PA559&dq=%22set+theories%22&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwjxnra5jY_cAhWIT7wKHV5QA_wQ6AEIYzAL#v=onepage&q=%22set%20theories%22&f=false|page=559
|passage=The one thing that all alternative '''set theories''' have in common is the fact that they are alternatives to ZF or ZFC.}}
# {{lb|en|music}} A [[systematic]] approach to describing musical objects and their relationships.
